Solve for a censoring-distribution parameter giving a target censoring fraction

Source: R/censoring.R
censoring_rate_for.Rd

Users think in terms of "about 20 end", not in the rate/scale units add_censoring needs, and the right units depend on the model's own time scale. This solves for one parameter of a fixed-family censoring distribution – the exponential/gamma rate, the Weibull scale at a fixed shape, or the lognormal meanlog at a fixed sdlog – that would give a target independent-censoring fraction, treating times – the event times from an already-run, uncensored simulation – as an empirical sample of the latent event time \(T\): it solves mean(F_C(times)) == target via uniroot, where F_C is the censoring distribution's own CDF (pexp/ pweibull/plnorm/ pgamma). This is the Monte Carlo estimate of \(P(C < T)\) under independence, using the supplied sample in place of \(T\)'s true (generally not closed-form once between-subject variability or covariates are in the model) distribution – approximate, and dependent on the run it is given: a different (even same-seed-different-n) uncensored run will give a slightly different answer. Re-check the realized fraction on a large cohort after drawing with the solved parameter; see vignette("pkpd-time-to-event", package = "simtte") "Right censoring" for a worked before/after check.

Usage

censoring_rate_for(
  times,
  target,
  dist = c("exponential", "weibull", "lognormal", "gamma"),
  shape = NULL,
  sdlog = NULL
)

Arguments

times

Numeric vector of event times (sim_status == 1 only) from an uncensored simulation. Must be non-negative and finite.

target

Numeric scalar in \((0, 1)\). The desired \(P(C < T)\).

dist

"exponential" (default), "weibull", "lognormal", or "gamma".

shape

Required (positive numeric scalar) for dist = "weibull" (solves for scale) or dist = "gamma" (solves for rate); the shape is fixed by the caller in either case. Unused otherwise.

sdlog

Required (positive numeric scalar) for dist = "lognormal" (solves for meanlog, with sdlog fixed by the caller). Unused otherwise.

Value

Numeric scalar: rate for dist = "exponential" or "gamma", scale for dist = "weibull", meanlog for dist = "lognormal".

Details

Only genuine event times are informative here: an administratively-censored subject's true \(T_i\) is unknown beyond end, so it carries no information about where independent censoring would actually bite. Pass times = events$sim_time[events$sim_status == 1] from an uncensored run, not the full events$sim_time.

See also

add_censoring, which takes the solved parameter in its censoring list; draw_censoring_times, to check the draws directly; sim_tte_ode, whose uncensored $events supply times.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = "exponential", param = list(H0 = 0.05),
  n = 500, end = 30, delta = 2, seed = 1)
#> Loading model from cache.
event_times <- sim$events$sim_time[sim$events$sim_status == 1]
rate <- censoring_rate_for(event_times, target = 0.2)
out <- add_censoring(sim$events, censoring = list(dist = "exponential",
  rate = rate), end = 30, seed = 2)
mean(out$sim_reason == "censored") # close to 0.2, on the events subset
#> [1] 0.24
# }
